blocks.task_summary: Find the median of a continuous random variable X with triangular PDF f(x) = 2(x-a)/((b-a)(c-a)) on [a,c] and f(x) = 2(b-x)/((b-a)(b-c)) on (c,b], given c ≥ (a+b)/2, in terms of a, b, c.
method_path: Recognise median m < c since c ≥ (a+b)/2, so m lies in [a, c]
Set up ∫_a^m f(x) dx = 1/2 or use triangle area ½ × base × height
Reject negative root since m > a, giving m = a + √((b−a)(c−a)/2)
accepted_alternatives: Geometric method: triangle area = ½ × (m−a) × [2(m−a)/((b−a)(c−a))] = (m−a)²/((b−a)(c−a)), set = 1/2

evidence.basis: M1 for attempting area of triangle or integration. A1 for base = (m−a) (geometric) OR A1A1 for correct integration and limits. A1 for area expression (m−a)²/((b−a)(c−a)). M1 for setting area/integral = 1/2. A1 for (m−a)² = (b−a)(c−a)/2 leading to ±√ form. A1 for rejecting negative root and final answer m = a + √((b−a)(c−a)/2).
